ChromSimPipe is the odd one out. It does not process sequencing reads; it runs physics
simulations on GPUs and compares them with Hi-C. That makes it the best place to see module 7:
outputs that are not single files, scatter-gather, and GPU resources.

Code on this page is pulled from the repository at the pinned commit (e32dd36).

## What the pipeline does {#cs-biology}

Cohesin folds chromosomes by loop extrusion: a cohesin ring loads on chromatin and reels DNA
into a growing loop until it falls off or stalls at a CTCF site whose motif points the right way.
Where cohesin stalls, and how long it stays, shapes the contact map you measure with Hi-C.
ChromSimPipe turns that idea into a test. It takes CTCF peaks (CUT&Tag or ChIP-seq) and a Hi-C
map, orients each CTCF site by scanning for the CTCF motif (JASPAR MA0139.1) with FIMO, and
simulates a polymer with loop-extruding cohesins (the Hansen lab's polysim, on polychrom and OpenMM)
over a genomic window.

Each *condition* in the config is one hypothesis: a set of cohesin parameters (lifetime, spacing,
stall probability at CTCF) plus a set of CTCF sites. The shipped example has three conditions that
ask whether the CTCF sites of a second state, alone or with weaker stalling, explain that state's
Hi-C. For each condition the pipeline turns simulated conformations into a contact map and compares
it with the experimental map (contact probability versus distance, loop pileups, insulation).

## The rule graph {#cs-rulegraph}

{{< generated name="chromsimpipe-rulegraph" >}}

<!-- GENERATE: chromsimpipe-rulegraph | pipelines/chromsimpipe | snakemake -s workflows/ChromSimPipe.snakefile --cores 1 --rulegraph -->

If the graph is missing above, it is because building it needs the input files (`data/` is empty
in the repository). In text, the order is the one in the header of the Snakefile:

{{< snippet repo="chromsimpipe" file="workflows/ChromSimPipe.snakefile" lines="4-24" >}}

`convertHic`, `getMotif` and `preparePolysim` run once and are shared by every locus. `orientCTCF`
and `validateCTCF` run per locus. Then the simulation fans out four ways (locus × condition ×
replicate × shard), `mergeShards` gathers the shards of each replicate, `analyzeCondition` gathers
the replicates of each condition, and `benchmarkSummary` collects the timings.

With the shipped config (one locus, three conditions, `n_replicates: 3`, `n_shards: 2`) that is
18 `simulateShard` jobs, 9 `mergeShards` and 3 `analyzeCondition`. <!-- VERIFY-DATA -->
The test config (one condition, one replicate, one shard) is the "10-job smoke test" the code
guide recommends running first on a new cluster. <!-- VERIFY-DATA -->

## A walk from inputs to outputs {#cs-walk}

1. **`ChromSimSamplesheet.txt`**: one row per experimental sample, with a `CTCF_Peaks` path and a
   `Hi-C` path (or `NA`) and free metadata columns. `fileNamesFrom: ['Condition']` names each sample.
2. **`config/ChromSimConfig.yaml`**: loci, conditions, physics (`polysim:`), motif settings, conda
   environments, job counts (`n_replicates`, `n_shards`), `outputDir`.
3. **`configs/parameters.py`** reads both and exposes everything as Python names.
4. **`convertHic`** converts each needed Hi-C map to `.cool` at the simulation resolution.
5. **`getMotif`** downloads the motif (only if no local MEME file is given); **`orientCTCF`** writes
   oriented CTCF sites per locus and CTCF sample; **`validateCTCF`** checks them.
6. **`simulateShard`** runs one polysim simulation on one GPU and writes HDF5 files of
   conformations into a shard folder.
7. **`mergeShards`** concatenates the shards of one replicate.
8. **`analyzeCondition`** computes contact maps and comparisons into
   `output/loci/<locus>/analysis/<condition>/`.

## Concepts in the wild

### Sentinel `.done` files, and why {#cs-sentinels}

{{< snippet repo="chromsimpipe" file="workflows/ChromSimPipe.snakefile" rule="simulateShard" >}}

The only declared output is `simulateShard_{condition}_rep{rep}_shard{shard}.done`. The real
result is a folder of HDF5 files under `sims/`, and the rule never names it: the script builds the
folder name itself, from the condition's `params_name` and `ctcf_type` and the replicate and shard
numbers (`<params_name>_ctcf-<ctcf_type>_rep<N>_shard<S>/`). Snakemake cannot track a path it is never
told. So the last line of the shell block, `touch {output.done}`, marks success. Because Snakemake
runs the block in strict mode, a crashed simulation stops before the `touch`, no marker appears,
and the job counts as failed.

Every downstream rule depends on markers, not data:

{{< snippet repo="chromsimpipe" file="workflows/ChromSimPipe.snakefile" rule="mergeShards" >}}

This is the gather half of a scatter-gather (module 7). The input is one marker per shard of this
replicate. `rules.simulateShard.output.done` is the *pattern* with `{locus}`, `{condition}`,
`{rep}` and `{shard}` still in it, and `expand()` fills all four: three from the job's own wildcards
and `shard` from `range(N_SHARDS)`.

What markers cost you, compared with `directory()` outputs:

- Snakemake does not delete a stale shard folder before rerunning a job, as it would for a declared
  `directory()` output. A rerun writes into whatever is there.
- Snakemake cannot tell whether the folder still exists. Delete `sims/` by hand and the markers
  still say everything is done. The troubleshooting notes in the repository say exactly this: if
  the merged folder is missing, delete its `.done` marker and resubmit.
- `--summary` and `--list-changes` describe the markers, not the data.

What they buy: the scripts own their folder layout, and adding a new analysis output to
`run_analysis_all.py` needs no change to the workflow (the code guide says so in "Adding new
analysis").

`preparePolysim` uses a marker for a different reason:

{{< snippet repo="chromsimpipe" file="workflows/ChromSimPipe.snakefile" rule="preparePolysim" >}}

polysim compiles part of itself (Cython) the first time it is imported. If 18 shards started at
once, they would all compile at the same time into the same place. This rule does the import once,
and every shard lists its marker as an input, so shards start only after the build exists. The
marker stands for "a side effect has happened", which no file output can express.

### The fan-out: locus × condition × replicate × shard {#cs-fanout}

{{< snippet repo="chromsimpipe" file="workflows/ChromSimPipe.snakefile" lines="160-165" >}}

`rule all` asks for one `analyzeCondition` marker per locus and condition. Everything else is
pulled in backwards: each condition marker needs `N_REPLICATES` merge markers, each merge marker
needs `N_SHARDS` shard markers. Change `n_shards` from 2 to 4 and the number of GPU jobs doubles
while each one saves half as many frames (`frames_per_replicate` is split across shards).

{{< snippet repo="chromsimpipe" file="workflows/ChromSimPipe.snakefile" lines="73-80" >}}

`L()` and `LP()` are small helpers worth copying. In `L()`, the f-string `{{locus}}` produces a
literal `{locus}`, so `L('done')` is a pattern with a wildcard in it. That is the same escaping as
MicroCPipe's `{{group}}` inside `expand()`, for a different reason: here it is f-string braces, not
`expand()` braces. `LP()` gives the concrete folder for a job's locus.

{{< snippet repo="chromsimpipe" file="workflows/ChromSimPipe.snakefile" lines="94-97" >}}

The constraints here are regexes, not name lists: a locus is anything without a slash, replicate
and shard are digits. `parameters.py` refuses locus names that contain `/`, which is what makes
`[^/]+` safe.

### An input function that adds an ordering {#cs-ordering}

{{< snippet repo="chromsimpipe" file="workflows/ChromSimPipe.snakefile" rule="analyzeCondition" >}}

Three inputs, three input-function patterns:

- `merged` gathers the replicates of this condition (as in `mergeShards`).
- `mcool = compare_mcool` returns the converted Hi-C map for this condition, or an empty list when
  the condition has none. An empty list is a valid input: it just adds nothing.
- `reference` returns another condition's `analyzeCondition` marker, but only when the config asks
  every condition to reuse one reference condition's calibration. This makes the rule depend on
  another job of *the same rule*, which forces an order without any file passing between them.

Note `--skip-existing` in the command. The script skips a replicate whose contact map already
exists. Combined with markers, that means deleting `analyzeCondition_<condition>.done` reruns the
job, but the job may then skip the work. Delete the analysis output folder too if you want it
recomputed.

### GPU jobs from the profile {#cs-gpu}

The `simulateShard` rule says nothing about GPUs except `--gpu 0`. The request is in the profile:

{{< snippet repo="chromsimpipe" file="profiles/slurm-template/config.yaml" lines="37-44" >}}

`gpu: 1` is a standard resource the SLURM executor plugin turns into `--gpus=1`, and the comment
records what did not work on one cluster (a `gres` request that was never submitted). The rule
can always say device 0 because, on a typical SLURM setup, a job only sees the GPU it was given.

The local profile handles the laptop/workstation case differently:

{{< snippet repo="chromsimpipe" file="profiles/local/config.yaml" lines="1-19" >}}

`resources: - gpu=1` is a *global* limit: the whole run has one GPU, and each `simulateShard` job
claims it (`set-resources: simulateShard: gpu: 1`), so only one simulation runs at a time while
other rules still run beside it. To test on a machine with no GPU, the config's
`polysim: platform: CUDA` can be set to `CPU`.

ChromSimPipe's SLURM profiles set `cpus_per_task` instead of `set-threads`, and the rules have no
`threads:` at all. The analysis parallelizes with `analysis.n_jobs` from the config, and the profile
comment says to keep `cpus_per_task` at least that large. Two numbers in two files that must agree
is the price of keeping resources out of the rules.

### `parameters.py`: one source of truth for Snakemake and scripts {#cs-parameters}

{{< snippet repo="chromsimpipe" file="configs/parameters.py" lines="1-32" >}}

In MicroCPipe and TTpipe, the Snakefile reads the config and passes values to scripts on the
command line. ChromSimPipe has dozens of physics parameters, and the simulation and analysis scripts
need most of them. Instead of passing them all as arguments, everything reads one module:

{{< snippet repo="chromsimpipe" file="workflows/ChromSimPipe.snakefile" lines="29-44" >}}

- Lines 33-35: the Snakefile loads the default config only if no `--configfile` was given. Normally
  Snakemake *merges* a `configfile:` in the Snakefile with `--configfile` on the command line. Here
  the author wanted the command-line file to replace the default completely, because the scripts
  read one file.
- Lines 36-37: the chosen file's absolute path goes into `$CHROMSIM_CONFIG`.
- Lines 39-44: the Snakefile imports `configs.parameters`, which reads `$CHROMSIM_CONFIG` itself.
- The per-locus rules set `CHROMSIM_CONFIG` and `CHROMSIM_LOCUS` in front of the script call
  (see `simulateShard` above), so each script imports the same module and sees the values for its
  own locus.

The module also validates more than either other pipeline does, with messages that say how to fix
the problem:

{{< snippet repo="chromsimpipe" file="configs/parameters.py" lines="107-118" >}}

The trade-off is that Snakemake no longer sees the values. Two consequences:

- **Changing a physics parameter does not rerun anything.** `simulateShard` passes only the config
  file's *path* as a param, so Snakemake's params rerun trigger sees no change, and the config file is
  not an input. The repository's troubleshooting table says it plainly: "Parameter changed but
  nothing reruns ... delete the markers for the steps to redo".
- **`--config key=value` does not reach the scripts.** It changes Snakemake's `config` dictionary,
  which the Snakefile uses for a few things (`resolution`, the motif, the conda envs), while
  `parameters.py` and every script read the file. `--config n_shards=4` changes nothing, quietly.

### A parse-time write that respects the cluster {#cs-parse-time}

{{< snippet repo="chromsimpipe" file="workflows/ChromSimPipe.snakefile" lines="99-110" >}}

The Snakefile writes a copy of the parsed samplesheet next to the outputs. The comment points at a
detail most people learn the hard way: on a cluster, *every job* parses the Snakefile again. An
unconditional write would rewrite the file from every job at once. Comparing first means it is
written once. (It also means `snakemake --lint` and `-n` write this file; parse-time code always
runs.)

### Conda environments: a file, a name or a path {#cs-conda}

{{< snippet repo="chromsimpipe" file="workflows/ChromSimPipe.snakefile" lines="55-60" >}}

`conda:` accepts an environment file, or the name or path of an existing environment. The config
allows all three, so a cluster where building the GPU environment is slow can point at one built
by hand. The `abspath` line handles a quirk: a relative `.yml` path in `conda:` is resolved from
the Snakefile's folder (`workflows/`), not from the repository root.

### A rule that exists only if needed {#cs-conditional}

{{< snippet repo="chromsimpipe" file="workflows/ChromSimPipe.snakefile" lines="188-204" >}}

Same pattern as TTpipe's `if TRIM:`. With a local MEME file in the config, there is no download rule,
and `MOTIF_MEME` points at the local file, which then has to exist. The shell block checks that the
download is really a MEME file, with the `|| {{ ...; exit 1; }}` form from module 4, because a web
server can return an error page with status 200.

### Testing {#cs-tests}

ChromSimPipe's tests are unit tests: `tests/test_parameters_config.py`, `test_loci.py` and
`test_paths.py` import `parameters.py` with small temporary configs and check paths, loci and
validation messages. There is no dry-run test and no CI workflow for the tests (the only workflow
publishes the docs). The test config is the substitute: one GPU job end to end, run by hand on a new
cluster.

## What you would change {#cs-change}

- **Put the condition's parameters into `params:`.** For example
  `params: cond = lambda w: COND_LOOKUP[w.condition]` in `simulateShard`. Snakemake stores params
  and reruns a job when they change, so editing `ctcf_capture` would rerun that condition's shards
  and everything after them, without anyone deleting markers.
- **Add a dry-run fixture and a CI job.** A tiny samplesheet and config under `tests/`, as in
  MicroCPipe and TTpipe, would let a dry run assert the 10-job and 39-job counts.
  <!-- VERIFY-DATA -->
- **Declare the merged folder as `directory()`.** Its name is known in the Snakefile
  (`merged_<params_name>_ctcf-<ctcf_type>_rep<N>`, all from `COND_LOOKUP`), so `mergeShards` could
  declare it and Snakemake would clear it before a rerun.
- **Make `getMotif` a local rule** (`localrules: getMotif`). It downloads from the internet, and
  compute nodes on some clusters have no outside network.
- **Keep account names out of shipped profiles.** `profiles/longleaf` and `profiles/pioneer` carry
  real SLURM accounts; the other two pipelines ship `<account>` placeholders and a launcher check.

## Exercises for the curious {#cs-exercises}

1. Add a second locus to `loci:`. How many more jobs does a full run have, and which jobs are not
   repeated?
2. You lower `ctcf_capture` for `cond2_weak-ctcf` and resubmit. What runs? What would you delete
   to get the right result today?
3. Rewrite `mergeShards` to declare its merged folder with `directory()` instead of a marker. What
   do you gain, and what new problem appears for `analyzeCondition`?
4. Why does `preparePolysim` not need a `{locus}` wildcard, while `validateCTCF` does?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Short answers

1. Per locus: 2 `orientCTCF` (one per CTCF sample), 1 `validateCTCF`, 18 `simulateShard`,
   9 `mergeShards`, 3 `analyzeCondition`, so 33 more jobs. <!-- VERIFY-DATA --> `convertHic`,
   `getMotif`, `preparePolysim` and `benchmarkSummary` are shared and still run once.
2. Nothing reruns: the markers exist, and nothing Snakemake tracks changed. Delete the
   `simulateShard_cond2_weak-ctcf_*`, `mergeShards_cond2_weak-ctcf_*` and
   `analyzeCondition_cond2_weak-ctcf.done` markers for that locus, *and* that condition's analysis
   folder (because of `--skip-existing`), then resubmit.
3. Snakemake now knows the merged data exists, clears it before a rerun, and `--summary` reports it.
   But `analyzeCondition` reads the merged folders through `--results-dir` (the whole `sims/`
   folder), so you would also want its input to name those folders, or the dependency is only on
   paper. The shard folders would still need markers unless you give them the same treatment.
4. The polysim build is the same for every locus, so it runs once. `validateCTCF` checks the CTCF
   sites inside one locus window, which differ per locus.
:::
